summary: Confirmed the sole recorded estimate, s2_creativity_high_vs_low_ai_dependence. PDF p. 5 prints the actual Study 2 sample of 132 participants, 66 per group; no exclusions or different analysis sample are reported. PDF p. 6, Table 2 and Section 3.3, print high-dependence M = 4.78, SD = 0.66; low-dependence M = 5.20, SD = 0.53; t(130) = 4.03, p < 0.001, and Cohen’s d = 0.70. The same page explicitly prints total effect c = −0.42. This is the overall contrast; the mediator-adjusted direct effect, indirect effect, and indirect-effect interval are correctly excluded. The positive printed t and d use the opposite direction to treatment minus control, as the extraction explains. Confirmed question, construct, measure, unit, higher_is, AI availability, timing, within-person coding, comparison type, and se_basis against the procedure and scoring description: both randomized groups used ChatGPT during the AUT, with different use instructions; trained psychology graduate raters supplied the creativity index, analyzed between participants. Read all 445 lines of the markdown conversion, including end matter and references, and checked the cited PDF pages with pymupdf. The PDF has 15 pages and no embedded supplement or appendix. No confirmed eligible outcome or contrast is missing. Study 1 is a nonrandomized self-report survey; the other Study 2 measures are questionnaires, and separate AUT dimension results are not printed. Study 3 remains unresolved as already documented in the extraction: the methods describe an unnamed AI trust-game manipulation and call the later AUT identical to Study 2 without explicitly specifying its AI availability or arm-specific instructions. Its full-sample Table 4 coefficients were checked, but eligibility cannot be established without those instructions. No local supplement is listed. Attempts to retrieve the MDPI supplement and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles and fullTextXML endpoints using the required User-Agent all failed with WinError 10013. The empty problems list confirms the recorded estimate and identifies no demonstrable omission in the available paper; it does not resolve Study 3 eligibility.
